key_decisions.ma_choice: One global prescaler that produces a single-cycle tick enable every PRESC+1 clocks, shared by all channels and held at 0 while GEN=0.
key_decisions.plan_choice: One global 16-bit prescaler that ticks every PRESC+1 clocks, is fanned out to all channels and is held at 0 while GEN=0.
key_decisions.note: PRESC is a global CTRL field, so the spec effectively implies a shared prescaler.

key_decisions.decision: Handling of a PRESC change mid-count
key_decisions.ma_choice: Any write to CTRL clears presc_cnt_q, so the new PRESC applies from a clean count. This restarts the current tick for all channels.
key_decisions.plan_choice: PRESC applies immediately against the live value. A >= compare wraps the counter at once if PRESC is lowered below it. CTRL writes do not clear the counter.
key_decisions.note: Both avoid the 2^16 long-tick lock-up. Only the plan avoids disturbing the tick phase on unrelated CTRL writes (e.g. GEN toggles).

key_decisions.ma_choice: Software-visible preload registers plus internal active registers for PERIOD, DUTY and CENTER, copied at the period boundary. Reads return the preload value.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Preload plus active shadow, loaded at the boundary. Reads return the last software-written preload.
key_decisions.note: The spec mandates shadowing but not which value is read back. Both chose the preload.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Counter runs 0..PERIOD-1, so the period is exactly PERIOD ticks. The boundary is the wrap to 0 and the output is active while cnt < DUTY.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Counter runs 0..PERIOD-1 and wraps, giving exactly PERIOD ticks. The boundary is the wrap and the output is active for DUTY ticks from the start.
key_decisions.note: The spec leaves PERIOD vs PERIOD+1 open.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Counter goes up 0..PERIOD-1, holds at the top, goes down to 0 and holds at the bottom, giving a symmetric 2*PERIOD ticks. Active while cnt >= PERIOD-DUTY, so exactly 2*DUTY ticks centred at the top. Boundary is only at the bottom.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Triangle 0 up to PERIOD and back down to 0 (2*PERIOD ticks) with no turning-point holds. Active while count > PERIOD-DUTY. Boundary and shadow load only at the bottom, pulse centred at the top.
key_decisions.note: Same architecture: up/down direction flag, single bottom boundary, pulse at the top. The plan's count range reaches PERIOD, so COUNT readback differs. Without holds, its compare does not obviously give exactly 2*DUTY symmetric ticks; this needs care at detailing.

key_decisions.ma_choice: The channel is treated as off (always inactive) regardless of DUTY. The counter holds at 0 and a boundary fires every tick.
key_decisions.plan_choice: The counter holds at 0 and every tick is a boundary. The output follows the DUTY rules: inactive if DUTY=0, otherwise always active.
key_decisions.note: Visible output differs for PERIOD=0 with DUTY>0 (active vs inactive). The plan is closer to a literal reading of 'DUTY >= PERIOD → always active'.

key_decisions.ma_choice: run = GEN & EN. Clearing either stops the channel immediately and the output goes to its inactive level the next cycle. Counter and dir are cleared to 0.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Immediate stop with output going to the POL level next cycle. Counter and dir are cleared while stopped. Re-enable starts a fresh period at 0.

key_decisions.ma_choice: While !run the shadows load continuously from the preloads, so enabling uses the latest values without waiting for a boundary.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Shadows are transparent while stopped (load = ~run | boundary).

key_decisions.ma_choice: CENTER is shadowed. On shadow load dir resets to 0, so the new mode starts cleanly from the bottom.
key_decisions.plan_choice: A CENTER change at the boundary restarts the counter at 0 with dir=0 in the new mode.

key_decisions.ma_choice: POL is not shadowed and applies one cycle after the write, which may create one edge.
key_decisions.plan_choice: POL is not double-buffered and applies on the next cycle.

key_decisions.ma_choice: A single output flop per channel after compare, overrides, run gating and polarity XOR. Latency is 1 cycle.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Each pwm_out bit is driven directly by a flop combining compare, DUTY overrides, enable gating and POL. Latency is 1 cycle.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Async assert, sync deassert. All flops reset to 0, so outputs are low after reset.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Async active-low reset on all flops, with deassertion assumed synchronised externally. Everything resets to 0.
key_decisions.note: The plan places the deassert synchroniser outside the block. This is effectively the same.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Registered rdata with 1-cycle latency. Unmapped and reserved bits read 0. RO and unmapped writes are ignored. A simultaneous read and write returns the pre-write value.
key_decisions.plan_choice: rdata flop loaded on reg_rd. Unimplemented slots read 0 and ignore writes. COUNT writes are ignored. A same-cycle read returns the pre-write value.

key_decisions.ma_choice: NUM_CH (1-8) plus configurable CNT_W and PRESC_W (up to 16), with an elaboration check on NUM_CH.
key_decisions.plan_choice: NUM_CH (1-8) only. Counter and prescaler widths are fixed at 16 bits.
key_decisions.note: Minor generality difference with no effect on the register-visible behaviour at the defaults.

summary: The plan closely tracks the MA on almost every architectural decision: shared prescaler, preload/active shadow scheme with preload readback, edge-aligned 0..PERIOD-1 counting, immediate stop with counters cleared and transparent shadows, immediate POL, a single registered output, reset style and bus behaviour. One difference is material: for PERIOD=0 with DUTY>0, the plan drives always-active while the MA treats the channel as off. Two differences are equivalent. The plan handles a PRESC change with a >= wrap instead of clearing the prescaler on any CTRL write. Its center-aligned triangle counts to PERIOD without turning-point holds, which changes the COUNT range and makes exact 2*DUTY symmetry less certain. The only question asked (Q1) addressed a real gap in the spec.
